propositions: The outbound mapper's _assignee_resolver is currently injected as an undeclared attribute using try/except AttributeError and discovered via getattr with a silent non-authoritative fallback, creating maintenance risk and type-checking gaps.

Silent injection failure masks bugs: PR #120's Data Center adapter copied the getattr discovery into a class where the attribute was never set, making the entire authoritative branch dead code without runtime error.
The resolver parameter must be threaded explicitly through compute_update_fields and diff_canonical_fields to reach the resolve_assignee call site, replacing the attribute-injection block.

DC backend has two resolver lifecycles—a constructor-bound client resolver and per-issue core-supplied resolver—where the core must take precedence; the explicit parameter design preserves today's overwrite semantics.

The neutral OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee contract and both Cloud and DC implementers must accept an explicit assignee_resolver keyword parameter with None as the documented non-authoritative default.
All four attribute-assignment and getattr-discovery sites must be eliminated and replaced with declared typed parameters; no # type: ignore[attr-defined] comments should remain.
